Level model. Every `fx_` file carries 6.02 dB of slider headroom: SoundPool volume cannot exceed 1.0, so "100% is twice as loud as 50%" has to live in the files. The app plays them at half volume by default (`CueTable.ASSET_BOOST`) and the slider's upper half spends the headroom. On top of that the files are mastered 0 dB hotter than the previous build's loudest setting (pre-emphasis around 2.6 kHz, soft limiter at -0.5 dBFS, see `scripts/generate-android-sounds.py`). The in-app chime copies (`fx_chime_*`, also the notification channel sounds) are the desktop chimes plus 12.04 dB (checked above); the desktop originals stay untouched.

Why only 2 dB under the chimes: the margin is an audibility floor, not a target. The interface cues are also far shorter than the chimes (tens of milliseconds against several hundred), so at equal RMS they are perceptually quieter still. Measured on active-region RMS.

Promoted desktop auditions (boosted, otherwise untouched) average -30.0 dBFS active RMS, +2.0 dB relative to the interface set.

Scope: peak, onset, clean-end, format and clipping assertions apply to every `fx_` file; the duration, direction, centroid-order and chime-margin assertions apply to the synthesised interface cues only, because the promoted desktop cues are intentionally at desktop level and multi-click.
